next.name: GOLD CRYSTAL
next.headline: GOLD CRYSTAL: the ShinyHunters-linked extortion brand that steals cloud data through phone scams
next.in_short: GOLD CRYSTAL is Secureworks' name for a cluster tied to ShinyHunters and Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters. Vendors say it phones staff to take over SaaS accounts, steals the data, then demands payment.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as GOLD CRYSTAL. Its catalogue record lists the aliases Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters, ShinyCorp, ShinyHunters and UNC6240.
SOCRadar says ShinyHunters, also known as ShinyCorp, is an international threat group that first emerged in 2020. EclecticIQ assesses it is financially motivated.

Trustwave SpiderLabs says Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters appeared on Telegram in August 2025 and borrows the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$. It reads the brand as a situational alliance, not a formal merger.
Trustwave suggests fewer than five people drive the core operation. It bases this on writing patterns, emoji use and posting rhythm, and says the number cannot be known with confidence.
EclecticIQ assesses that ShinyHunters very likely relies on members of Scattered Spider and The Com to carry out voice phishing.

Okta's threat team says a cluster it calls O-UNC-053, previously assessed as affiliated with ShinyHunters, may have rebranded. A new leak site called INCEPTION has listed its data. INCEPTION denies any ShinyHunters link, and the exact relationship is unknown.
Trustwave says the brand focuses on cloud data theft from SaaS and CRM platforms. FalconFeeds, citing other vendors, reports over 1,500 breaches across SaaS, retail and telecom.
EclecticIQ says attackers took Salesforce datasets from airline and retail enterprises. ReliaQuest ties 2025 waves to retail, then insurance, then aviation.
ReliaQuest says domain analysis suggests financial services and technology service providers are likely next targets.

Okta says the O-UNC-053 cluster has hit many sectors, including technology, healthcare, biotechnology, financial services, insurance, entertainment, gaming, retail, transportation, hospitality and legal.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group tracks a related cluster, UNC6040. It says the cluster phones employees while posing as IT support. It asks them to connect a modified Salesforce Data Loader to their company's Salesforce environment.
Google says UNC6040 then pulled Salesforce data and in some cases moved sideways into other platforms. Extortion sometimes came months later.
Google reports that the actors claimed to be ShinyHunters. Google says this is likely a way to raise pressure on victims.
EclecticIQ says the group impersonated Okta single sign-on login pages to steal credentials. It also says the group recruited insiders and used AI-driven voice calls.
Resecurity reports the group abused OAuth tokens tied to Salesloft and Drift integrations to reach Salesforce environments.
Okta says the O-UNC-053 cluster uses phone calls and a phishing kit to capture credentials and MFA approvals. The landing page is tailored to the target's identity provider.
Trustwave says the brand announced an extortion-as-a-service model. It says a claimed Sh1nySp1d3r ransomware is still unverified.
Resecurity reports that ShinyHunters claimed a data breach at Qantas in July 2025.
On 12 September 2025 the FBI issued a FLASH alert linking Salesforce breaches to UNC6040 and UNC6395, according to Picus. Picus says the group announced on 17 September that it was going dark.
Resecurity does not believe the announced retirement is sincere. Another report says claims that the group stopped intrusions could not be independently verified.

Cybersecurity Dive reports that Workday confirmed a social engineering campaign. Attackers reached customer contact details through a third-party support vendor. Workday said it saw no sign its own servers were accessed. The report links the activity to ShinyHunters and Scattered Spider.

The Hacker News, reporting Okta's findings, says the ShinyHunters leak site went offline in late September 2026 after the arrest of alleged members. INCEPTION began listing data on 16 November 2026. Unit 42 reported over 70 legal-themed lookalike domains since October 2026.
Train help desks and staff to verify any caller who asks them to approve an app connection, share a code or accept an MFA prompt.
Group names keep changing, so build defences around the tactics rather than the label.
